label: <DEL> step when the sequence is rich in f/o/j/z (and c/p/0/3)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (86% of activations, 92% of activation mass); essentially silent during the original phase, with weak residual firing on early copy steps (mostly recall_idx 2). Only about 11% of <DEL> steps are active. Which ones depends on the token makeup of the original sequence: it acts like a weighted sum over the tokens seen, with f, o, j, z weighted most (next_out/prev2_tok lift 5-6x for f/o) and c, p, 0, 3 weighted less. Top examples are short sequences made almost entirely of f/o/j (e.g. o o j j <DEL>, f f f <DEL>). Shorter L gives a higher rate. Requiring at least half the original tokens to come from {f,o,j,z,c,p,0,3} gives dev F1 0.46 (P 0.43, R 0.49, mass recall 0.63). A looser threshold of one third raises mass recall to 0.87 but lowers precision to 0.26. The binary set rule is only an approximation of what looks like a graded, token-weighted signal, so precision and recall both stay incomplete.
